examples.title: UK domain, US provider, data hosted in India
examples.summary: A service on a .uk domain, run by a US-headquartered company, storing its data on servers in India. Three jurisdictions touch the same data, so the assessment scores their combined exposure as one profile.
explainer: Each component takes the highest exposure across the three jurisdictions. India sets Judicial Oversight and Transparency, the UK sets Technical Requirements, and the US sets Extraterritoriality, because a US parent company can be compelled to produce data wherever it is stored. All three score 80 for Agency Powers.

Together they score 83, higher than any one of them alone (the UK scores 67, the US 69 and India 71), because each brings its own worst feature. Use the Perspective panel to see how it changes for where you are asking from.

rationale.JO: India's interception and decryption orders are made by the Union or state Home Secretary and reviewed only by officials, with no prior judicial approval. The UK scores 50 and the US 70.
rationale.AP: All three score 80: bulk or programme-level collection with compelled provider assistance, through UK bulk warrants, US Section 702 and Executive Order 12333, and India's broad grounds under the IT Act and Telecommunications Act.
rationale.TR: UK technical capability notices can require a provider to remove electronic protection it applied, and the 2024 amendments add advance notice of security changes. India scores 80 and the US 45.
rationale.EX: The US CLOUD Act reaches data held by US companies wherever it is stored, and Section 702 reaches any provider with access to communications equipment. The UK scores 65 and India 45.
rationale.TP: India publishes no statistics on interception or decryption orders and does not notify people. The UK scores 55 and the US 40.
rationale.EI: No comprehensive embargo applies between these three jurisdictions.
rationale.SS: Low exposure unless customers or counterparties appear on sanctions lists.

examples.title: The Deep Dive reference vector
examples.summary: The illustrative vector used in the Deep Dive's Vector Notation section. It is not tied to a particular country; it shows how embargo exposure interacts with the legal base score.
explainer: The base score is 72 and Embargo Impact is 70. The GLARS score takes the higher of the two, and because the embargo is itself in the High band, the overall level would be High even if the base score were lower.

examples.title: Strong oversight, no trade restrictions
examples.summary: An illustrative profile for a jurisdiction with independent prior judicial authorisation, targeted rather than bulk powers, published transparency statistics and no embargo or sanctions exposure.
explainer: These values are illustrative and do not describe a specific country. They show what a Low result looks like: the base score drives the outcome because both trade components are close to zero.
